clue.text: Child's toy spooked Alice, unfortunately

indicators.note: things gone unfortunately have gone wrong, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

parts.note: the twelve letters of these two words are the fodder for the rearrangement

explanation.surface: Something frightened Alice, and that was unfortunate for her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spooked' reads as part of the story but is simply anagram fodder alongside Alice.
explanation.definitionFit: A tube of mirrors and coloured beads is a classic plaything for children.

clue.text: King has advantage, a light anchor

parts.note: an edge over someone is an advantage

explanation.surface: A king holds the upper hand, perhaps at sea with a small anchor.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the nautical term for a small anchor used for warping a ship along.

clue.text: Member of City guild — a disagreeable chap?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a freeman of one of the City of London livery companies
second meaning, read whimsically: a 'livery' (irritable, liverish) man

explanation.walkthrough: The City is the City of London, whose ancient trade guilds are called livery companies. 'Livery' also means bad-tempered, as if from a sluggish liver; the question mark flags this joke reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A freeman of a London trade company wears its livery, hence the title for its members.

clue.text: Universal hospital doctor at Scottish island loch

parts.note: an intern is a junior doctor working in a hospital
taken as written
Iona is a small island in the Inner Hebrides

explanation.surface: A junior doctor works somewhere by a loch on a Scottish island.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spanning all nations is worldwide, near enough a synonym for universal.

clue.text: Piece of fruit in William III's house

definitions.meaning: second meaning: William III was William of ..., of the royal House of ...

explanation.walkthrough: William III, king of England from 1689, came from the Dutch House of Orange-Nassau.
explanation.definitionFit: The citrus fruit shares its name with the Dutch royal dynasty from which William III came.

clue.text: Trick girl into scattering a lot of stars

parts.note: to con someone is to trick them
Stella is a girl's name

indicators.note: scattering the letters of the word into rearranges them

parts.note: the four letters of this little word are the ones scattered

explanation.surface: A conman tricks a girl into scattering lots of stars, a fairground scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A grouping of stars forming a recognised pattern in the night sky, like Orion.

clue.text: Take aim at earthenware vessel

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to take a shot at it

explanation.walkthrough: To take a pot shot, or pot at a target, is to aim casually at it.
explanation.definitionFit: The short word is both a verb for shooting at something and a noun for a ceramic container.

clue.text: Treacherous type initially without support

indicators.note: initially asks for only the opening letter of the word without

parts.note: only its first letter is wanted, giving the opening of the answer
an easel is a stand that supports a painting

explanation.surface: A traitor is left at the start with no support.
explanation.definitionFit: A sly, untrustworthy person is called after the cunning animal, an idiom for a sneak.

clue.text: Part of bedding of the French surgeon

parts.note: du is French for 'of the'
a vet is an animal surgeon

explanation.surface: A French surgeon's bedding is under discussion.
explanation.definitionFit: A quilt stuffed with down or feathers is a standard element of a bed.

clue.text: Girl using stake to secure mesh?

indicators.note: the stake holds the mesh fast by wrapping around it

parts.note: the ante is the stake put up in poker
a net is a mesh

explanation.surface: A girl uses a post to pin down some netting, perhaps in the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a female first name, a diminutive of Anne.

clue.text: Slip up, with some improper response

indicators.note: some of the phrase improper response is used, its letters running across the word gap

parts.note: the run of letters spans the end of improper and the start of response

explanation.surface: Someone blundered by giving an unsuitable reply.
explanation.definitionFit: To blunder or make a mistake, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Accuracy of intelligence, abandoning leading bishop!

indicators.note: the word loses the bishop letter that leads it, at the front

parts.note: brightness is cleverness or intelligence

explanation.surface: An exclamation that cleverness is accurate once a top bishop departs.
explanation.definitionFit: Correctness or exactness of a statement is a near synonym of accuracy.

clue.text: Evergreen trees given faulty clue? A pity

indicators.note: a faulty arrangement means these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A solver complains that a defective crossword clue is a pity.
explanation.definitionFit: Gum trees of Australia keep their leaves all year; this is the Latin plural.

clue.text: Dance a doctor introduced to South America

indicators.note: being introduced to the region puts the pieces inside its letters

parts.note: taken as written
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A doctor arrives in South America and meets a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively Brazilian ballroom and carnival dance.

clue.text: Note about spies in party, perhaps

indicators.note: the note goes about, around the spies

parts.note: sol is a note of the sol-fa scale
the CIA is the US spy agency

explanation.surface: A message mentions spies attending a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A social is a friendly gathering, of which a party is one kind; 'perhaps' marks the example.

clue.text: Laughing out loud with accountant in pub

indicators.note: the accountant sits in the middle of the laughing letters

parts.note: LOL is texting shorthand
CA is a chartered accountant

explanation.surface: Someone guffaws with their accountant over drinks in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' is British slang for one's neighbourhood pub.
explanation.definitionFit: The bar nearest home that one regularly visits is called one's local in British usage.

clue.text: Asian writer upset boxer

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the word upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: a pen writes
Muhammad Ali, the boxer

explanation.surface: An author from Asia has upset a boxer.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Nepal, the Himalayan country in Asia.

clue.text: Spanish wine shop accommodating the French vocal style

indicators.note: the shop takes in, accommodates, the French article

parts.note: a cantina is a Spanish bar or wine shop
le is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: A Spanish bodega makes room for a French singing style.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantilena is a smooth, lyrical melodic line in singing, a musical term.

clue.text: Beat young farm animal endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a lamb is a young sheep

explanation.surface: Someone keeps on hitting a baby animal on the farm.
explanation.definitionFit: To lam is an informal verb meaning to thrash someone.

clue.text: Episcopal headgear finally cast in mud

indicators.note: the letter is placed in the mud

parts.note: mire is mud or bog

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the word cast

parts.note: its final letter is the one placed in the mud

explanation.surface: A bishop's hat ends up thrown down in the mud.
explanation.definitionFit: The tall pointed hat worn by bishops, episcopal meaning of bishops.

clue.text: A Liberal bar, one attracting a European state

parts.note: taken as written
to ban is to bar
taken as written

explanation.surface: A political party's bar draws in someone from a European country.
explanation.definitionFit: The Balkan country on the Adriatic, a nation of Europe.

clue.text: Hanger-on starts to be unreasonably resolute

indicators.note: the starts of the three words are taken

parts.note: the first letters of these three words spell the answer

explanation.surface: A clinging follower begins to dig in unreasonably.
explanation.definitionFit: A bur is a prickly seed head that clings to clothing, hence figuratively a clinger.

clue.text: Contribution from fashionable place

parts.note: in means in fashion
to put something is to place it

explanation.surface: A donation comes from a trendy venue.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's input is what they contribute to a discussion or project.

clue.text: Fine diamond, possibly, in English hair oil

parts.note: a brilliant is a finely cut diamond, and brilliant also means fine
taken as written

explanation.surface: A diamond turns up in some English hair oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Brilliantine is a scented oil used to make hair glossy, a dated grooming product.
